title: KV compact-slice allocator and temporal-churn smoothing for GPU memory
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Introduce a compact-slice allocator for KV cache that reduces long-tail fragmentation by packing small live KV entries into contiguous slices and applying a temporal-churn smoothing policy. Goal: reclaim fragmented GPU memory without causing latency regressions to generation p95s during continuous batching workloads. This ticket covers design, simulator experiments, runtime implementation, telemetry, and a controlled canary rollout.

Motivation: Current fragmentation patterns show many small free holes caused by token churn and short-lived conversational prefixes. Background compaction either interferes with serving or requires large memory headroom. Compact-slice combines opportunistic in-place packing for low-cost reclaim with a time-windowed smoothing policy to avoid repeated relocations of hot keys.

Design overview:
- Allocation unit: introduce a compact-slice (micro-contiguous region) layer between KV logical pages and GPU physical segments. Slices are sized (configurable) to 512B-8KB depending on observed token footprints.
- Packing policy: live entries below a slice-size threshold are opportunistically moved into underutilized slices during low-latency-safe windows (e.g., between batch dispatch cycles).
- Temporal-churn smoothing: keys with high churn (many writes in short window) are tagged with a cooling period; the scheduler defers packing/relocation until they stabilize, preventing thrash.
- Eviction synergy: integrate with existing eviction watermarks so packed slices are preferred for eviction to create larger free spans.
- Non-blocking relocation: use copy-on-write KV indirection with short-lived write locks to avoid blocking reads; relocations are batched and rate-limited by token latency budget.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reduce measured fragmentation (lost allocable memory due to <1MB holes) by >=35% for chat workloads in staging.
- P95 token generation latency increase <= 5% during normal traffic and <=10% during canary at 10% traffic.
- No increase in error rates or KV corruption incidents.
- Telemetry surfaces slice utilization, relocation rate, cooling-window violations, and memory reclaimed per hour.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulator experiments and offline replay (done)
2) Implement in runtime behind feature flag + unit/integration tests
3) Staging canary on 5% traffic with telemetry dashboard and automatic rollback trigger (p95 > +10% or error spike)
4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring and operator runbook

Risks and mitigations:
- Relocation thrash causing latency spikes: mitigate with cooling windows and relocation rate cap.
- Unobserved correctness edge cases: heavy fuzz tests + cross-checks in dev/staging with synthetic KV invariants.
- Interaction with quantized kernels & memory allocator: coordinate with infra allocator team and include low-level leak tests.

Notes: design doc and replay traces attached in links. Experimental simulator config and scripts are in the runtime repo under /tools/kv-sim/compact-slice.
comments: 2026-02-11 — Aisha Patel: Initial spike analysis completed. Found median hole size ~2.3KB across chat workloads; waste dominated by many small holes. Uploaded analysis spreadsheet to Drive.

2026-02-15 — Marco Nguyen: Prototype allocator simulator implemented (tools/kv-sim). Baseline vs compact-slice run shows ~42% reduction in tiny-hole fragmentation on conversation replay dataset (N=12k sessions). Latency model predicts <3% p95 impact when relocation rate <= 200 ops/s per GPU.

2026-02-20 — Design review notes (PM + Infra): Consensus to prefer opportunistic packing between batch dispatch windows and to expose config knobs for slice size and cooldown. PM asked for SLO-safe rollout gates and customer-facing FAQ draft.

2026-02-26 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1357 — Adds compact-slice allocator and relocation scheduler behind feature flag 'kv_compact_slice_v1'. Includes unit tests and basic telemetry counters.

2026-03-01 — Telemetry MVP: Added metrics: slice_count, slice_utilization_pct, relocations_total, relocations_rate, cooling_violations, memory_reclaimed_bytes. Dashboard draft: https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-frag. Early staging shows relocations_rate ~50/s and memory_reclaimed 1.2GB/hour on a 80GB cache instance.
2026-03-03 — Marco Nguyen: Integration tests passed. Noted one flaky test under heavy simulated churn; root cause: race in cooler timer; fix committed in PR update. Re-running CI.

2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel: Plan to enable canary on staging cluster next week (2026-03-09). Canary guardrails: auto-disable if p95 > +10% for 5m or if error rate doubles. Added runbook section with rollback steps and contact matrix.
Follow-ups: add eviction preference heuristics, experiment with variable slice sizing per-tenant, and add a compact-slice read-only fast-path to reduce indirection overhead.
